advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Rename `_is_closed` in `_ready.py`/`_unblock.py` to reflect terminal semantics (e.g. `_is_terminal`) now that it accepts archived/deleted.
evidence: The predicate membership is now `frozenset({"closed", "archived", "deleted"})` (src/rebar/types.py:347), so `_is_closed("archived")` returns True despite the name.
advisory.finding: After the change, the helper `_is_closed` in `_ready.py` and `_unblock.py` delegates to `is_terminal_status`, so it now returns True for `archived` and `deleted` statuses, not just `closed`. The name no longer describes what it computes, which can mislead maintainers reading the blocker logic.
scenarios: A future maintainer reading `all_blockers_closed`/`ticket_is_closed` assumes only status == 'closed' unblocks and reasons incorrectly about archived/deleted handling.
advisory.suggested_fix: Rename the local `_is_closed` helpers to `_is_terminal` (or inline `is_terminal_status`) in `_ready.py` and `_unblock.py` and update call sites, so the name matches the widened membership.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that an ARCHIVED blocker causes detect_newly_unblocked/batch_close_operations to report the dependent as newly-unblocked, covering the archived widening at the _unblock.py call site.
evidence: _unblock.py diff removes `_CLOSED_STATUSES = {"closed", "deleted"}` and routes `_is_closed` through `is_terminal_status`, adding `archived`
search of tests/ for detect_newly_unblocked returns only tests/scripts/test_ticket_unblock.py (pre-existing) — none in the new parity file
tests/scripts/test_ticket_unblock.py:586-680 test_batch_close_excludes_archived asserts on open_children, not on an archived BLOCKER unblocking a dependent via _is_closed
New test file tests/interfaces/queries/test_terminal_blocker_parity_e63c.py exercises only rebar.ready, next-batch CLI, and deps CLI (lines 92-108) — no _unblock surface
advisory.finding: The behavior change to graph/_unblock.py (detect_newly_unblocked's _is_closed now treats `archived` as terminal, previously {closed, deleted}) is one of the four unified call sites but is exercised by no test in this change. The new parity test file only drives rebar.ready, `next-batch`, and `deps` (_graph.py); none call detect_newly_unblocked or batch_close_operations. The pre-existing tests/scripts/test_ticket_unblock.py::test_batch_close_excludes_archived asserts open_children exclusion (the exclude_archived path), not that an ARCHIVED blocker now yields a newly-unblocked dependent — the specific regression this diff introduces at that site. Widening _unblock's terminal set to include archived could regress silently.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a case to tests/scripts/test_ticket_unblock.py building blocker→blocked with the blocker driven to ARCHIVED, asserting detect_newly_unblocked returns the blocked id (RED before the archived widening).

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Verify the archived-blocker next-batch case exercises the `archived` membership (not the 'closed' status-map default); assert on the actual resolved status or use a fault-isolating setup that would fail if archived were dropped from TERMINAL_STATUSES.
evidence: next_batch.py:180,229 use `ticket_status_map.get(d.get("target_id", ""), "closed")` — default 'closed' for any target not in the map
An archived blocker is excluded from the open/in_progress list and is not tombstoned, so it resolves to the 'closed' default, which is_terminal_status already accepted pre-change
test_ready_and_next_batch_agree_on_an_archived_blocker (lines 147-155) would pass on the 'closed' default irrespective of the archived widening
advisory.finding: The archived-blocker parity test for next-batch may pass via the ticket_status_map 'closed' default rather than actually resolving 'archived', so it is a weak regression guard for the next_batch call site specifically. In next_batch.py the status map is built only from open/in_progress tickets (line 145-151) plus tombstone overrides; an archived ticket is neither open/in_progress nor tombstoned, so `ticket_status_map.get(target_id, "closed")` falls back to 'closed' — already terminal even before this change. The assertion would hold whether or not `archived` was added to TERMINAL_STATUSES for next_batch.
